To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human visual system can be modeled as a set of linear operators that transform a given light field into the perceived light field and that the display device should be capable of generating light fields that are perceptually indistinguishable from the perceived light field.

1) the light field is a fundamental concept that needs to be extended to the human visual system in order to account for its physiological requirements, and 2) this extension is called the perceivable light field and it provides a fundamental analytical framework for the 3-D displays to match the human visual system requirements.
